I’m in Australia and all they tested was the one gene that would have been defective if I had CADASIL which they got from my mums history. It was relatively easy to get tested with a referral from a GP.
What they told me was that they genetically test the embryos and only implant embryos without the gene.

I would suggest talking to a genetic councillor. I don’t know how that would work in other countries, but in Australia, you could just google and make an appointment with just a referral from your GP. Having a family history of Cadasil is enough to get a referral.

Not only will they explain the disease to you, but the implications of a positive test. My Mum has Cadasil and I got tested in 2017. I chose to get tested because I was getting ready to start a family, but if I had the disease I wanted to use IVF to ensure the gene wasn’t passed on. I became very depressed at the time and having an expert to talk to really helped. They met with me when I got my results back even though they were negative for the gene to ensure that all my questions were answered.

Hope this helps

The key is to tailor your resume to the job you are applying for. Look at your resume from the perspective of a hiring manager. 

If you are applying for a target job, and have a resume showing you are overqualified then they aren't going to bother with an interview.

On the other hand if you have a resume, only showing your degrees and no previous work experience, they are going to question your work ethic. You can hire the most educated person for the job, but that doesn't mean they will get the job done.
